law: REGISTRATION of E-Q27 — does the ternary zero do work? (ORCH-R25 lane T16-c; the prior-art pass's open question Q3). Binary ({-1,+1}), ternary ({-1,0,+1}, the E-Q22 rule), and 4-level (quaternary, quartile-based) quantizations of BOTH sealed arms (score-continuous S and noul-continuous N), same live retrieval protocol, arm-filtered queries (the metadata-index law applied from the start this time). ZERO new embed calls. The question: is the ternary middle level carrying information beyond the sign, and where does quantization-diminishing-returns set in?
provenance_of_the_question: The research pass (R24-RESEARCH): the retrieval-code literature is overwhelmingly BINARY at 100s-1000s of bits; an untrained 8-coordinate ternary QA-code at 16 bits is unoccupied territory, and whether the ZERO level does work is the sharpest open sub-question (Q3). E-Q22 found ternary retention 86% (score arm) / 69% (noul arm) vs continuous — the binary and 4-level points on the same curve are missing.

design_frozen.arms: S (E-Q21 sealed score vectors) and N (E-Q22 sealed noul vectors), 20 records each
design_frozen.quantizations: BINARY: x > m_a -> +1 else -1 (the sign, no zero; m_a = the E-Q22 median rule). TERNARY: the E-Q22 AM1-registered rule (+1 if x > m + 0.5*MAD, -1 if x < m - 0.5*MAD, else 0). FOUR-LEVEL: quartile thresholds q25/q50/q75 per axis over the 20 corpus values -> {-1.5, -0.5, +0.5, +1.5}. All tables derived from the arm's own 20 corpus vectors only, frozen in the results file.
design_frozen.eval: Six arms upserted (eq27SB, eq27NB, eq27ST, eq27NT, eq27SQ, eq27NQ; the metadata arm field set, arm-FILTERED topK 20 queries — no topK starvation by construction); top-1 non-self WITHIN-ARM family accuracy, STRICT scoring only (NO-NEIGHBOR impossible under the arm filter; receipt if any)
design_frozen.measures: accuracy per quantization per arm; the zero-level mass (fraction of 0s in ternary codes); monotonicity checks (B vs T vs Q vs continuous); the ternary-zero information question: among records whose ternary code contains >= 1 zero, does binary (which forced that axis to +/-1) misfile them more?

floors.F1: vectors are the sealed E-Q21/E-Q22 vectors, recomputed from the sealed rows
floors.F2: quantization tables derived from the arm's own 20 corpus vectors only, frozen pre-eval
floors.F3: all six arms upserted with metadata arm tags AND live-queried through arm-filtered topK

hypotheses.H1_zero_works: T > B on at least one arm (the zero level carries retrieval information beyond the sign)
hypotheses.H2_diminishing: Q - T < T - B on the arm where H1 holds (diminishing returns above 3 levels) OR Q <= T on both arms (4 levels buy nothing)
hypotheses.H3_saturation_interaction: the T-B gap is larger on the N arm (saturated noul mass produces more zeros; more zeros = more value from the zero level)
hypotheses.C22: the ternary zero does work — LIVES iff H1

predictions.P1: T > B on both arms by >= 0.05 (one record)
predictions.P2: Q within 0.05 of T on both arms (4 levels buy little at 20 records)
predictions.P3: zero-level mass on N (mean ~0.35-0.5 of axes) exceeds S (mean ~0.25-0.4)
predictions.P4: continuous still beats every quantization on both arms (quantization only ever costs)

falsifier: ANY of F1-F4 breached; a quantization table computed from anything but the arm's own corpus vectors; an arm queried without the filter (the E-Q24 receipted trap); scoring on anything but denominator 20.
